- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to compensate for sentiment-driven risk premium.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — if 30d forecast is > 85, reduce by 2–5% to align with recent 18d mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 75, model often overestimates; apply downward bias of 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
